personas.name: Specialist-Trade Subcontractor Owner
personas.icp: Owner-operator of a 5-30 staff M&E, renovation or specialist-trade subcon doing project work for main-cons and developers; cashflow runs on progress claims and 5-10% retention.
pains: Main-cons pay 60-120 days late and dispute claims to delay payment
Retention sums quietly withheld or never released after defect-liability period
No way to know a main-con's payment reputation before signing the LOA
Bad-faith variation disputes used as leverage to shave the final account
personas.current_workaround: Asks other subbies in the same trade WhatsApp groups whether a main-con pays; gut feel and word-of-mouth only.

nba.summary: One avoided late-pay or retention chase saves ~2.5h/mo of owner admin and calls at S$45/h owner time.

personas.name: SME Credit-Control Manager
personas.icp: Finance or credit-control manager at a 20-150 staff SME who approves trade-credit limits and payment terms for new B2B accounts.
pains: Vetting a new account before extending terms relies on a thin ACRA filing snapshot
Financial statements lag 12-18 months and hide current payment behaviour
Existing aged-debtors only show how a customer pays YOU, not the market
Pressure from sales to approve terms fast with no peer signal to push back on
personas.current_workaround: Pulls an ACRA Business Profile (~S$5.50) plus an ad-hoc commercial credit report when the limit is large; otherwise approves on sales' say-so.

nba.summary: Substitutes part of a recurring DP/Experian commercial-report spend with peer payment signal for routine accounts.

personas.name: Wholesale / Trade-Credit Distributor
personas.icp: Wholesaler or distributor (FMCG, building materials, electronics) shipping stock on 30-60 day trade credit to a long tail of resellers and retailers.
pains: Ships goods first, gets paid last; a single phoenixing customer wipes a month's margin
Long tail of small buyers too low-value to justify a S$40-60 credit report each
Customers vanish or rebrand under a new UEN leaving the invoice stranded
Sales-led onboarding extends credit before finance ever sees the account
personas.current_workaround: Extends a small starter limit on gut feel, watches first two payment cycles, then raises the limit; eats the occasional bad debt as cost of doing business.

nba.summary: Replaces occasional ad-hoc ACRA pulls plus grapevine checks with cheap per-lookup tokens across a long buyer tail.

personas.name: Mid-Market Procurement & Vendor-Onboarding Lead
personas.icp: Procurement or vendor-onboarding lead at a corporate or mid-market firm running supplier due-diligence and registration before a PO is raised.
pains: Onboarding checks cover incorporation and KYC but miss how a vendor TREATS counterparties
Legal-threat bullying and NDA/IP breach by suppliers surface only after a deal sours
Sourcing decisions made with no behavioural reputation signal, only price and references
Hand-picked vendor references are curated and never disclose disputes
personas.current_workaround: Runs KYC/sanctions screening plus an ACRA extract and requests trade references the vendor itself nominates; legal reviews contracts after issues appear.

nba.summary: Adds a behavioural-reputation line to an onboarding stack of KYC screening plus company-data lookups.

personas.name: Trade-Association Watchlist Administrator
personas.icp: Administrator or secretariat staff at a trade association or cooperative maintaining a shared members' watchlist of problem counterparties.
pains: Members repeatedly burned by the same bad-faith counterparties with no shared memory
Watchlist lives in spreadsheets and meeting minutes, impossible to query at point of deal
No defensible identity-keyed record to share without defamation exposure
Cannot offer members a tangible data benefit to justify membership renewal
personas.current_workaround: Circulates an informal blacklist by email and at members' meetings; relies on collective memory and committee word-of-mouth.

nba.summary: Org-level seat replacing a manual watchlist; benchmarked to a credit-bureau-style subscription amortised across the membership.

pricing_models.name: Per-lookup lemon tokens
pricing_models.rationale: Matches the spiky, event-driven nature of counterparty checks; ~S$0.03/check and ~S$0.10/comprehensive upload keep the first lookup near-free, undercutting a S$5.50 ACRA pull on a per-event basis and lowering activation friction.

pricing_models.name: Flat monthly subscription
pricing_models.rationale: Predictable cost for users who check regularly; converts grapevine habit into a budgeted line and smooths revenue, but over-prices the occasional checker.

pricing_models.name: Freemium self-check
pricing_models.rationale: A business checking its OWN score free (plus free appeals) drives identity claims and data correctness, seeds the graph, and creates a viral know-your-own-score loop; monetisation comes from checking OTHERS.

pricing_models.name: Tiered SME plans
pricing_models.rationale: Window Shopper / The Stall / The Orchard bundle monthly token allowances with depth features (history, alerts, comprehensive reports); good-better-best anchoring nudges credit teams up from per-token to a plan.

pricing_models.name: API / usage onboarding tier
pricing_models.rationale: Programmatic lookups for vendor-onboarding and association watchlists priced on volume; embeds Lemon Score in existing procurement and membership systems and unlocks the largest contract values.

elasticity_heuristics.evidence: Owner pays out of pocket and already gets word-of-mouth free; even S$10/mo is weighed against a free WhatsApp group, so demand drops sharply above ~S$10.
Already budget S$30-60 for commercial reports; a S$10-20 peer-signal add-on reads as cheap insurance, but it competes for the same vetting line and is dropped if utilisation is low.
Per-buyer value is low so any per-lookup price above a few cents kills coverage of the tail; token model thrives, subscription resisted.
Behavioural-reputation data is differentiated with no direct substitute in the onboarding stack; budget is departmental not personal, so a S$20-45/mo seat is rounding error against contract risk.
Org-level buyer amortises cost across members and frames it as a renewal benefit; value scales with membership, so a few hundred S$/mo is defensible and sticky.
Must stay free; any charge to view your own reputation triggers churn and undermines data-correctness incentives, so elasticity is effectively infinite at zero.

recommended_tiers.name: Window Shopper
what_in: Free check of your own Lemon Score
Free appeals on your own record
Basic public summary score on others
recommended_tiers.psychological_anchor: Knowing your own lemon score is free, the same way ACRA gives you your own profile free after a filing.

recommended_tiers.name: The Stall
what_in: Comprehensive report unlock at 3 tokens each
Email alert when a saved counterparty's score drops
recommended_tiers.psychological_anchor: Less than one S$5.50 ACRA profile per month, but you can check a whole trade's worth of counterparties.

recommended_tiers.name: The Orchard
recommended_tiers.psychological_anchor: A third of one S$30-60 commercial credit report per month, but it shows how a company treats its suppliers, not just its bank.

recommended_tiers.name: Grove API & Association
what_in: Programmatic lookup API with volume tokens
Bulk UEN screening for vendor onboarding
Defamation-safe identity-keyed records keyed to UEN and ACRA directors
what_excluded: Free-tier branding removal on member portals unless contracted
recommended_tiers.psychological_anchor: Less than a single mid-tier credit-bureau subscription, amortised across an entire membership instead of one finance desk.

grants.name: PSG (Productivity Solutions Grant) — aspirational
grants.eligibility: CONDITIONAL / NOT YET SECURED. Applies only if Lemon Business is accepted as an IMDA/ESG pre-approved PSG solution, which it is not today. No PSG support exists until and unless that listing is granted.

grants.name: EDG (Enterprise Development Grant) — possible for association rollout
grants.eligibility: ASPIRATIONAL. An EDG project (e.g. an association digitalising a members' watchlist) could in principle defray the Grove API & Association tier, but requires a qualifying scoped project, ESG approval and an appointed consultant. None secured.

grants.name: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit (SFEC) — speculative
grants.eligibility: SPECULATIVE / NOT CONFIRMED. SFEC top-up can only offset out-of-pocket cost on a separately qualifying programme; it does not by itself make Lemon Business fundable and no eligibility has been established.
